title: Truly linear-time Laplacian solving
formal: Does one randomized algorithm, for every connected weighted graph and zero-sum right-hand side, return \(\widehat x\) satisfying \[\|\widehat x-x^*\|_L\le\tfrac1{10}\|x^*\|_L\] with probability at least 2/3 in expected \(O(m)\) total arithmetic operations, where \(Lx^*=b\)? The constant must be independent of the graph size and edge-weight ratios.
definitions:
The input is a connected simple undirected graph on n≥2 vertices, m edges given in adjacency lists, positive real weights w_e, and b∈R^n with sum zero. The weighted Laplacian has diagonal entries equal to the sum of incident weights and off-diagonal entry −w_uv for an edge, zero otherwise. The zero-mean solution x* is unique. Define \(\|z\|_L=(\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv}(z_u-z_v)^2)^{1/2}\). This seminorm ignores additive constants, so no normalization of the returned vector is necessary. If b=0, the required error is zero in this seminorm.

Editorial model choice: exact-real arithmetic RAM with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, square roots, comparisons, array access, and independent random O(log n)-bit words at unit cost. Every input read, preprocessing step and output write is charged. No matrix inverse or eigenvalue oracle is free. The algorithm terminates almost surely; its expected time is bounded on each fixed input, and the success probability is over its internal coins. The fixed accuracy 1/10 is part of the target, so dependence on arbitrarily small error is not requested. No condition-number bound or polynomial weight range is assumed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proofs of the uniform expected linear bound and energy-error probability, or a complete impossibility proof in the same model. A nearly linear bound containing an unbounded factor of log n or log log n does not meet O(m). Empirical linear scaling is insufficient.
context:
Laplacian solvers connect graph algorithms and numerical linear algebra. The requested improvement concerns removing all asymptotic overhead at fixed relative accuracy, including for poorly conditioned inputs.

Jambulapati and Sidford give a solver with an iterated-logarithmic overhead. That is very close to linear, but does not establish the strict linear bound asked here.
why: This asks whether approximate Laplacian solving can reach literal input-linear arithmetic complexity.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can a weighted graph Laplacian system Lx=b be solved to a fixed relative error, such as 1/10 in the L-energy norm, in expected O(m) arithmetic operations for an m-edge connected graph? This asks to remove the remaining logarithmic overhead from Miller’s line of nearly linear solvers.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The question assumes sum(b)=0 and measures relative error against the exact solution modulo the Laplacian nullspace; it concerns arithmetic complexity, not bit complexity.
